run.procedureSummary:
Step 1 (arrivals): add each cycle's new tickets to teams 1-6; no limits applied at this step.
Step 2 (walk): go team 1 to team 6 in order; any amount over a team's WIP limit (10, 8, 12, 6, 9, 7) is moved to the next team down and counted toward that team when you reach it; team 6's overflow goes to the closed tally.
Step 3 (status): after the walk, a ROUTINE team at or above its escalation mark (7, 6, 9, 5, 7, 5) becomes ESCALATED; an ESCALATED team at or below its stand-down mark (3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2) becomes ROUTINE; otherwise status holds. Every flip is logged.
Step 4 (work queues): use one snapshot of the step-3 counts. A ROUTINE team closes floor(n/4), which goes to the closed tally. An ESCALATED team removes floor(n/2) and bounces it to team i-1; team 1's bounce is closed. Bounced tickets may leave a team over its limit until the next walk, and after cycle 5 they stay.
Step 5 (backlog cut): total the board. If it is strictly over 38, each team keeps floor(n/2) and the rest is closed. At 38 or less, nothing changes.
Closed tally: starts at 0 and adds team-6 overflow, ROUTINE closures, team-1 bounces and backlog-cut closures.

openPoints.point: Step 4 when a team both sends and receives a bounce
openPoints.assumption: All closures and bounces come from the single step-3 snapshot and are applied together. Bounces a team receives are not worked off in the same step.

openPoints.point: Which counts the status check in step 3 uses
openPoints.assumption: The counts after the step-2 walk. States are tested once per cycle, and a team flips at most once per cycle.

openPoints.point: Excess passed down during the walk
openPoints.assumption: Excess is added to the next team before that team is checked against its own limit, so it can cascade further down. Team 6's excess is closed and counted on the tally.
Every quarter and every half is rounded down (floor), as the write-up says. For the backlog cut, the closed amount is the board total minus the sum of the floored halves.
The cut fires only when the total is strictly above 38. The cycle-5 total was exactly 38, so the cut did not fire.

openPoints.point: Arrivals over the limit at step 1
openPoints.assumption: 'Limits don't bite yet' is read as no cap during step 1. Limits are applied only in the step-2 walk.

run.balanceCheck: 20 tickets at start + 94 arrived = 114; 38 open + 76 closed = 114. The two sides match.

run.notes: I did the arithmetic with a short Python script in the scratchpad (g.py). The closed tally of 76 is made up of 5 from team-6 overflow, 23 from ROUTINE quarter closures, 1 from team-1 bounces and 47 from the backlog cuts (21 in cycle 1, 25 in cycle 4). After cycle 5, teams 2 (10 vs limit 8) and 4 (7 vs limit 6) stay over their limits because of bounced tickets, which the write-up allows.
